name: GMVN Tourist Rest House Gangotri
why_it_matters: The Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam (state tourism) lodge sits on the southern bank of the Bhagirathi, a few minutes from the temple. Its dining hall is the closest thing Gangotri has to a sit-down restaurant — pure-veg, predictable, and open through the May-October season.
insider_tip: Take breakfast outdoors when the morning sun hits the deck — guests describe aloo parathas with the Bhagirathi roaring into Surya Kund as the table soundtrack. Kitchen slows badly during yatra peak; order 30 min before you want to eat.
signature_address: GMVN Tourist Rest House, southern bank of Bhagirathi, Gangotri, Uttarkashi 249135

name: Saket Restaurant
why_it_matters: On the main road into Gangotri town, Saket is the recommended pick by repeat Char Dham travellers — the menu spans North Indian, South Indian and a few Garhwali specials at pilgrim prices. Generous portions and a balcony with valley views.
insider_tip: The lachcha and stuffed tandoori parathas with house chutneys are the dish locals point first-timers to — heavier than dosa for the cold mornings before the temple aarti.

name: Cafe Himalaya
why_it_matters: A small bistro-style room with a garden patch, a rare touch of cafe-format in a town built around dhabas. Pure-veg by Gangotri rule, but the menu reaches a little further than thali — paneer dishes, Indo-Chinese, hot drinks for cold pilgrim mornings.
insider_tip: Best as a mid-morning stop after temple darshan, not dinner — kitchens in Gangotri close early once the bus pilgrims clear out.

name: Ganga Niketan
why_it_matters: One of the cluster of pilgrim-thali kitchens lining the lane down to the Bhagirathi temple. Honest dal-chawal-roti from a single open kitchen, Garhwali home-style, served fast to the post-darshan crowd.
insider_tip: Eat between 11am and 1pm when the dal is freshest — by 4pm everything is reheated. Cash only; no cards on this stretch.
signature_address: Temple Road, near Gangotri Mandir, Gangotri, Uttarkashi 249135

name: Panchpuri Sadan
why_it_matters: Another temple-lane bhojanalaya, named after the puri-halwa offering many pilgrims eat after darshan. Bench seating, copper bell on the door, the same five rotating dishes every Char Dham season — utility, not ambience.
insider_tip: Closes the moment Gangotri does — usually by Diwali. From November to April the shutter stays down, so don't trust offline guidebooks during winter trips.
